common_name: Bush Early Girl Tomato (Compact Container Slicer)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into full sun after danger of frost has passed; this compact determinate selection needs no staking beyond a small cage.

directions: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil once nights stay reliably above 50F, or grow directly in an 18-24 inch container. Bush Early Girl is an All-America Selections winner bred as a true determinate, space-saving counterpart to the classic indeterminate Early Girl, staying under 30 inches tall while still producing full-flavored, 6-8 ounce red slicing tomatoes only a few days later than its parent. Its short, sturdy frame makes it a favorite for patios, raised beds, and small gardens where staking a full-size vine is impractical, and it carries verticillium and fusarium wilt resistance for reliable production.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant into a large pot or garden bed after frost danger passes; a very short, stocky plant that thrives in patio containers as small as 12 inches across.

directions: Sow indoors and transplant into a sunny patio container or garden bed once frost danger has passed, keeping the compact plant evenly watered since small pots dry out quickly. Patio, an early All-America Selections winner, was one of the original dwarf tomato hybrids bred specifically for container growing, staying under 24 inches tall while still bearing clusters of 3-4 ounce round red fruit with reliable, old-fashioned tomato flavor. It remains a benchmark heirloom-era patio variety that predates the many modern compact hybrids it inspired.

common_name: Husky Cherry Red Tomato (Compact Cherry Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then transplant after frost danger passes; a stout, dark-stemmed dwarf plant that produces heavily in containers or small beds with only light staking.

directions: Transplant into full sun after the last frost, giving the sturdy, thick-stemmed vine a small cage to support its heavy cherry tomato clusters. Husky Cherry Red is an All-America Selections winner in the Husky series bred for a compact, potato-leaf indeterminate habit that concentrates energy into abundant 1-1.5 inch, deep-red, sweet-tart fruit rather than excess vine growth, making it a dependable choice for smaller gardens that still want continuous cherry tomato production. It is distinct from the larger-fruited Husky Red slicer in the same series.

common_name: Window Box Roma Tomato (Compact Paste Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors about 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant into a window box, patio pot, or small bed after frost danger has passed.

directions: Transplant into a sunny window box or small container after the last frost; the plant stays extremely compact, so it needs no staking or cage even when loaded with fruit. Window Box Roma is an All-America Selections winner bred to bring true plum-shaped paste tomatoes to the smallest growing spaces, producing 1.5-2 ounce oblong red fruit with meaty, low-moisture flesh well suited to sauces despite the plant's diminutive 12-18 inch stature. It offers one of the few genuinely dwarf paste-tomato options for balconies and windowsills.

common_name: Lizzano Tomato (Trailing Cherry Tomato for Hanging Baskets)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant into a hanging basket or rail planter after frost danger passes, letting the trailing stems cascade over the container edge.

directions: Transplant into a hanging basket or rail-mounted container after the last frost and let the trailing stems spill downward rather than staking them upright. Lizzano is an All-America Selections winner noted for combining a true cascading habit with strong early blight tolerance, an unusual pairing that keeps foliage healthier through the season than most basket-type tomatoes. It produces abundant clusters of sweet, 1-inch red cherry tomatoes continuously from mid-summer until frost.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into full sun once soil has warmed, after all danger of frost has passed.

directions: Transplant into full sun once the soil has warmed, growing it as either a landscape edging plant or a container specimen. Flaming Flare is an All-America Selections winner grown as much for its upright, torch-like clusters of small fruit that shift from purple to yellow to orange to red as it matures as for its edible use, giving a single compact plant several color stages at once. The fruit carries mild-to-moderate heat and can be harvested for cooking at any color stage, making the plant genuinely dual-purpose in the garden.

common_name: Cornito Rosso Pepper (Sweet Red Mini Snack Pepper)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm, fertile soil in full sun after frost danger has passed.

directions: Transplant into full sun after the soil has warmed, staking lightly if the compact plant becomes heavy with fruit. Cornito Rosso is the red-ripening companion to the yellow Cornito Giallo, an elongated, tapered mini pepper bred for sweet, thin-walled flesh that is equally good eaten fresh as a snack or quickly pan-fried whole. Fruits ripen to a glossy deep red about a week later than the yellow type and hold well on the plant for a long harvest window.

common_name: On Deck Sweet Corn (Compact Container Corn)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed to at least 65F; because plants stay short, block-plant even a small number of stalks in a large container or short row for reliable wind pollination.

directions: Direct sow in blocks of at least four rows, even in a large container, once the soil has warmed to ensure adequate cross-pollination between the short stalks. On Deck is an All-America Selections winner bred specifically for small-space and container gardening, reaching only about 4-5 feet tall while still producing two 7-8 inch bicolor ears per stalk with classic sweet corn flavor. Its shrunken stature makes it one of the few sweet corn varieties genuinely practical for a patio or deck planter.

planting.note: Direct sow as soon as the soil can be worked in spring, 2-4 weeks before the last frost; because each seed produces a single seedling, thinning is rarely needed.

directions: Direct sow thinly in early spring or late summer, since each seed ball contains only a single embryo and germinates as one seedling rather than the tangled cluster typical of most beets. Moneta is an All-America Selections winner valued for this true monogerm trait, which eliminates the tedious thinning normally required for beets and makes precision seeding practical for both home gardeners and small-scale growers. It produces smooth, uniformly round, deep-red roots with sweet flavor and tender greens suitable for salad mixes.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, or direct sow once soil has warmed.

directions: Transplant into full sun after the last frost and pinch flower spikes regularly to prolong leaf production through summer. Aromatto is an All-America Selections winner bred to combine deep, glossy purple foliage with the robust, spicy-sweet flavor of a true Genovese-type basil, filling a gap left by most purple basils, which tend toward milder, clove-like flavor. Its vigorous upright habit and strong aroma make it useful both as a culinary basil for pesto and vinegars and as an ornamental accent in the herb bed.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant 2-4 weeks before the last frost for a spring crop, and again in late summer for a fall crop; can be grown at tight spacing in containers because of its small mature size.

directions: Direct sow in early spring or late summer, thinning or transplanting to close spacing since mature heads stay compact. Bambi is an All-America Selections winner bred as a true miniature romaine, forming dense, upright 6-inch heads with sweet, crisp leaves in about half the space and time of standard romaine, and it holds quality and resists bolting notably longer as temperatures rise. Its small size also makes it well suited to container growing and to serving as an individual single-portion salad head.
